{{Short description|Formula for spinors}}
The '''Lichnerowicz formula''' (also known as the '''Lichnerowicz–Weitzenböck formula''') is a fundamental equation in the analysis of [[spinor]]s on [[pseudo-Riemannian manifold]]s.  In dimension 4, it forms a piece of [[Seiberg–Witten gauge theory|Seiberg–Witten theory]] and other aspects of [[gauge theory]]. It is named after noted mathematicians [[André Lichnerowicz]] who proved it in 1963, and [[Roland Weitzenböck]]. The formula gives a relationship between the [[Dirac operator]] and the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] acting on spinors, in which the [[scalar curvature]] appears in a natural way.  The result is significant because it provides an interface between results from the study of [[elliptic partial differential equation]]s, results concerning the scalar curvature, and results on spinors and spin structures.

Given a [[spin structure]] on a pseudo-Riemannian manifold ''M'' and a [[spinor bundle]] ''S'', the Lichnerowicz formula states that on a [[section (fiber bundle)|section]] &psi; of ''S'',
:<math>D^2\psi = \nabla^*\nabla\psi + \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{Sc}\psi</math>
where Sc denotes the [[scalar curvature]] and <math>\nabla^*\nabla</math> is the [[Lichnerowicz Laplacian#Connection Laplacian|connection Laplacian]].  More generally, given a [[complex spin structure]] on a pseudo-Riemannian manifold ''M'', a [[spinor bundle]] ''W''<sup>±</sup> with section <math>\phi</math>, and a connection ''A'' on its [[determinant line bundle]] ''L'', the Lichnerowicz formula is

:<math>D_{A}^{*}D_{A}\phi=\nabla _A^{*}\nabla_{A}\phi+\frac{1}{4}R\phi+\frac{1}{2}\langle F_{A}^{+},\phi\rangle.</math>

Here, <math>D_A</math> is the [[Dirac operator]] <math>D_A:\Gamma (W^+)\to \Gamma (W^-),</math> and <math>\nabla _A</math> is the [[covariant derivative]] associated with the [[connection (vector bundle)|connection]] A, <math>\nabla _A: \Gamma (W^+)\to \Gamma(W^+\otimes T_M^*)</math>. <math>R</math> is the usual scalar curvature (a contraction of the [[Ricci curvature|Ricci tensor]]) and <math>F_A^+</math> is the [[self-dual]] part of the curvature of A. The asterisks denote the adjoint of the quantity and the brackets <math>\langle , \rangle</math> denote the [[Clifford algebra|Clifford action]].
